Thanks — useful framing. Mapping the four assumptions to what this PR actually changes:

**1 & 4 (ULID / imported ids):** agreed, that's the root cause — and it's exactly what this removes. `latest()` and the loop-exit now key on `time.created`, with the id only as a same-millisecond tiebreaker, so an imported id that sorts high no longer masquerades as the newest message.

**2 (same millisecond):** already covered for natively-minted ids — `Identifier.create()` packs `timestamp * 0x1000 + counter` (a monotonic per-ms counter), so two messages in the same ms still sort in creation order via the id tiebreaker. For imported sessions `time.created` is authoritative. The only unrecoverable case is an importer that collapses every message to a single timestamp *and* emits non-monotonic ids — at that point the ordering information is gone in the data itself; no consumer-side comparison can reconstruct it (an importer bug). I deliberately did **not** use array position as the tiebreaker: `filterCompacted` reorders the array (`compaction-user, summary, …retained tail…, continue-user`), so position isn't chronological — which is the whole reason `latest()` scans for the max instead of trusting order.

**3 (compaction rewriting ids):** compaction mints fresh ids via the same `ascending()` (so their embedded time is current), and `latest()` already derives by max time/id specifically to survive that reorder. I've added a regression test — `survives compaction: array is reordered and messages are rewritten with new ids` — that builds a compaction-reordered history with rewritten ids and asserts the newest user/assistant/finished still resolve by time, not position.

On the broader point: you're right that comparing message order to decide loop termination is a heuristic, not a proof. This PR makes the heuristic correct for every case the data can actually support. A fully ordering-independent exit (track that *this* iteration produced a finished assistant with no pending tool calls, rather than comparing last-user vs last-assistant) is a larger change — happy to open it as a follow-up so it can be reviewed on its own merits. This PR stays the minimal, behavior-preserving fix for the reported infinite loop, with the failing→passing regression test as the precondition.

On the testing questions: the change is deterministic ordering logic in `latest()` and the loop-exit precondition — it never inspects the provider, model, context size, or token rate, so those axes don't affect its correctness, and the id tiebreaker preserves current behavior for natively-minted ids so native sessions can't regress. The things that *do* matter — the ordering itself and compaction — are covered by unit tests: the original failing→passing regression (the loop precondition), plus a new compaction-reorder test that exercises a reordered array with rewritten ids.

For a deterministic invariant like "the newest assistant must resolve after the newest user," a targeted unit test is a stronger proof than a stress run (a stress run only samples the timestamp distributions it happens to hit; the unit tests pin the exact adversarial orderings). Happy to add more orderings if there's a specific one you'd want covered.

Worth noting this isn't import-specific. The four issues flagged as the same `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` root cause — #38787, #28618 (client/server clock skew), #29478 (web-client-generated ids), #30809 — include native, non-import repros (#28618, #29478). So the fix addresses a recurring, multiply-reported class, not just third-party imports.

(Setup, since you asked: the `@ai-sdk/anthropic` provider against a LiteLLM gateway. The loop reproduced deterministically on an imported session whose message ids weren't time-sortable — which is exactly what the regression test encodes, so it fails on `main` and passes with the change independent of model or load.)

Superseded: f599f8f3d3 already landed this on v2 with a better shape — a `#runtime-plugin-support` conditional import (Bun implementation + node stub) at the top of the plugin provider, which installs before any external plugin import and doesn't hard-throw under node like this entrypoint import would. Closing.

I also reviewed the existing [`opencode-openai-compact`](https://github.com/partment/opencode-openai-compact) plugin. It demonstrates that native compaction can be implemented through plugin hooks and is a useful opt-in path. The proposed core behavior is narrower and keeps fallback state in the existing session model rather than an auxiliary checkpoint database.

Current core behavior:

```text
manual /compact
  -> compaction agent
  -> local text summary
  -> session history
```

Proposed core behavior:

```text
manual /compact
  +-> POST /responses/compact
  |     -> validate one encrypted compaction item
  |     -> persist canonical output on the compaction part
  |
  `-> existing local summary
        -> durable fallback if remote compaction or later binding fails

later OpenAI Responses turn
  -> verify provider + model + endpoint + credential binding
  -> replace the completed local boundary with canonical output
  -> append only post-compaction turns
```

The proposed scope is:

- direct OpenAI Responses sessions only;
- manual `/compact` only; automatic compaction remains local;
- API-key and ChatGPT OAuth compact routes;
- strict response validation and scoped replay;
- the existing local summary lifecycle always completes and remains recoverable;
- no replay after a model, provider, endpoint, or credential switch.

I would keep `previous_response_id`, WebSocket protocol changes, request compression, compatible-provider aliases, and automatic `context_management` out of the change.

If maintainers prefer plugin-only support, I am happy to leave this in plugin space. If core integration is welcome, I can open a focused PR after the private implementation has soaked in daily use.

> Confirmed the same root cause on Windows 11 (PS 7.6.3, opencode 1.17.9 via mise/node). The Expand-Archive autoload fails only when spawned from the Bun-compiled binary, works perfectly when run manually from either powershell.exe or pwsh.exe.
> 
> Looking at the compiled source, opencode searches for rg.exe in this order:
> 
> 1. rg.exe anywhere in PATH
> 2. rg.exe directly at `~/.cache/opencode/bin/rg.exe`
> 3. Download the ripgrep zip and extract it with `powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "$global:ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'; Expand-Archive ..."`
> 
> Step 3 is where it breaks. The workaround is to short-circuit at step 2:
> 
> ## opencode already downloaded the zip to ~/.cache/opencode/bin/
> $zip = "$env:USERPROFILE\.cache\opencode\bin\ripgrep-15.1.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip"
> 
> # Extract rg.exe manually (avoiding Expand-Archive autoload entirely)
> Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
> $archive = [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::OpenRead($zip)
> foreach ($entry in $archive.Entries) {
>     if ($entry.FullName -match 'rg\.exe$') {
>         $dest = Join-Path (Split-Path $zip) "rg.exe"
>         [System.IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::ExtractToFile($entry, $dest, $true)
>     }
> }
> $archive.Dispose()
> ## Clean up the zip (no longer needed)
> Remove-Item $zip -Force
> After this, restart opencode. It finds rg.exe at step 2 and never calls Expand-Archive. The glob and grep tools work without errors.

@krlosgarciar is right. You can send this to your opencode and let it fix the bug for you:  
Run this PowerShell command to bypass the Expand-Archive autoload bug (issue #24291). It extracts rg.exe from the already-downloaded ripgrep zip using the .NET API instead of Expand-Archive, so opencode finds rg.exe at step 2 and never calls the broken module.
```powershell
$zip = "$env:USERPROFILE\.cache\opencode\bin\ripgrep-15.1.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip"
$dest = Join-Path (Split-Path $zip) "rg.exe"
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
$archive = [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::OpenRead($zip)
foreach ($entry in $archive.Entries) {
    if ($entry.FullName -match 'rg\.exe$') {
        [System.IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::ExtractToFile($entry, $dest, $true)
        break
    }
}
$archive.Dispose()
Remove-Item $zip -Force
```
Then **#restart#** opencode. grep/glob/skill tools will work without the Expand-Archive error.

Thanks for working on GHES support. I reproduced the current failure with OpenCode 1.18.9 and the pinned official GitHub Action on a GHES runner. The runner provides an internal GITHUB_API_URL, but github.handler.ts constructs Octokit without a baseUrl, so the GHES token is sent to api.github.com and the run fails with 401 Bad credentials.

This PR addresses that REST failure, but I noticed the GraphQL client currently receives ghUrls.apiUrl as its baseUrl. On GHES, GITHUB_API_URL normally ends in /api/v3. @octokit/graphql appends /graphql and documents the GHES baseUrl as https://host/api, so using the REST URL would target /api/v3/graphql instead of the GHES endpoint /api/graphql. GitHub Actions also provides GITHUB_GRAPHQL_URL.

Could getGitHubURLs return a separate GraphQL base URL, using GITHUB_GRAPHQL_URL with the trailing /graphql removed, and fall back to serverUrl + /api for GHES? A focused request-mocking test that asserts the final REST and GraphQL URLs would also catch this distinction.

I can validate an updated branch against the GHES dry-run that exposed the 401. I have omitted the private host and credentials from this report.

Thanks for writing this RFC. We implemented the core dispatch idea locally against OpenCode v1.17.9: an explicitly configured agent can route `task(subagent_type=...)` to an external CLI instead of creating an LLM child session.

The patch is intentionally small and touches three files. The config schema and runtime `Agent.Info` each gain `command?: string` and `external?: boolean`, and the task tool gains the dispatch branch. When `agent.external && agent.command`, it runs `Bun.spawn(["sh", "-c", command])`, pipes the task prompt through stdin, collects the process result, and bypasses the child-session pipeline entirely. This keeps the feature inert unless both fields are configured.

A few implementation details were easy to get wrong:

* The prompt needs to go through stdin, not a positional argument. With CLIs that accept variadic options such as `--allowedTools`, a trailing prompt can be consumed as another option value.
* Session flags need to be conditional: use `--session-id` for a new external session and `--resume` for continuation, never both.
* Interactive tools such as `AskUserQuestion` do not work under noninteractive `-p` execution, so they need to be explicitly disabled. We use the subscription auth path and do not inject credentials into the adapter.

Our source patch has been reviewed and its dispatch path verified at code level, but we have not deployed the binary. The build is currently blocked by a pre-existing Bun v1.3.14 Effect schema regression, unrelated to these changes.

Would a PR using this schema-based, opt-in approach be welcome, perhaps as a smaller precursor to the full protocol and conformance layer proposed here? For the dispatch result, is there an existing event-envelope and artifact format you would prefer us to target rather than returning a task result directly?

Happy to contribute a PR aligned with the extension boundary and result contract you prefer.

One implementation detail that may prevent this panel from showing ghost agents: make it a projection of a durable execution ledger, not just the live event stream. Each row needs a stable `run_id` / `agent_id`, parent identity, explicit lifecycle transitions, a heartbeat timestamp, and a terminal result; otherwise a disconnect can leave an agent looking `running` forever even though its process completed or died.

VOLY's A2A canvas uses this pattern: nodes are upserted from `pending` to `running`, then `completed` / `failed` / `blocked`, with route, duration, cost, files, error, and heartbeat-backed run records: https://github.com/voly-codes/voly/blob/main/docs/backend/a2a.md

For the proposed read-only first PR, I'd include `stale` as a distinct display state even if restart/cancel controls come later. It preserves honest observability without expanding the initial scope.

Confirmed on macOS with OpenCode Desktop 1.18.9 after renaming a Git repository and using **Close
 project → Add project** with the new path.

   Old path:

   `/Users/xx/Sites/projects/content`

   New path:

   `/Users/xx/Sites/projects/blog`

   OpenCode retained the session history, but new sessions would not launch.

   A read-only inspection of `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` showed:

   - `project.worktree` still referenced the deleted old path
   - `project_directory.directory` contained the correct new path
   - `project.sandboxes` contained the new path
   - both paths were associated with the same project ID
   - `PRAGMA integrity_check` returned `ok`

   The logs showed repeated failures resolving the deleted path:

   `PlatformError: NotFound: FileSystem.realPath (...)`, caused by `ENOENT`.

   This matches the root cause described in #39056: `Project.fromDirectory()` retains `existing.worktree`
 even when that path no longer exists, while the new path is added as a sandbox. Desktop navigation then
 resolves the sandbox back to the stale primary worktree.

   This is still reproducible in 1.18.9.
